Research/2025-26/Planetary engineering

Planetary engineering

Building a Tumbleweed Rover for Mars

A lightweight wind-driven rover prototype and an initial attempt to scale terrestrial test results to Mars.

Research question

What did the project ask?

Can a lightweight, wind-driven rover prototype be built and tested on Earth, then scaled to estimate performance under Martian conditions?

Significance

Why does it matter?

A simple, low-cost wind-driven rover could make distributed planetary exploration more practical.

Method

What did the team do?

The team constructed a PEX-B frame with 3D-printed joints and fabric sails, measured its travel speed against wind speed, and explored gravity and atmospheric-density scaling for Martian conditions.

Principal result

What did the evidence show?

Earth tests showed rover speed increasing approximately linearly with wind speed, with the poster reporting R-squared = 0.88. The retained artifact does not support a reliable quantitative statement about predicted Martian speed.
